\n and consumes no quota. Omitting the header is read as a request that declined\n to identify itself, and gets a fresh run ever
y time.\n* **Check `canceled` before reporting a failure.** A stopped run carries\n `status: \"failed\"`, because cancellation is
recorded as a marker rather than\n a status of its own. `stale: true` is the third case: the runner went silent\n and the watch
dog settled the run.\n* **`targetId`, not `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two environments can\n resolve to the same host with d

ifferent servers, so a run can hold two
 targets that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Launching **spends**: a run fans o
ut into `targets × iterations`\n> sessions. Two different `429`s can come back — the per-minute burst brake\n> (retry in seconds)
and your plan's daily launch cap (resets at UTC midnight).\n> Both normally carry `Retry-After`; back off on your own when one doe

s not.

**Swarms — insights** — what a run revealed. Read these in order of cost: the
roll-up and the scorecard are determinist

ic and free, the findings registry
aggregates them, and swarm run insights run a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
\n| `GET .../goals-overview` | Project roll-up: recent runs, goal-completion rates, repeat failures, trend |\n| `GET .../goal-runs
/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's deterministic rubric result. No model, no spend |\n| `GET .../goal-findings` | Criteria that keep
failing, tracked across swarm runs |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Hide a finding |\n| `POST .../goal-findings
/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide it |\n| `GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Poll a swarm run's generated insights. **40
4 = nobody asked** |\n| `POST .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Request them. `202` — scheduled, not done |\n| `DELETE .../s
warm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Cancel a generation still `pending` |\n\nTwo arithmetic traps worth naming, because both produc

e numbers that look
plausible and are wrong:

* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, never by the session total.** Three failures
 o
ut of four graded sessions, in a run that attempted forty, is 75% — not\n 7.5%.\n* **`failedGradingCount` is not `failCount`.** A

crashed judge is not a
 regression, and folding the two together makes one look like the other.

And one modelling note: a fi
nding's `status` is a lifecycle —\n`new | recurring | regressed | resolved`. `dismissed` is *not* one of them.\nDismissal is the o

rthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a finding can be both recurring
and dismissed, and hiding one never claims it stopped happening.

>

[!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swarm run insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on
> MCPJam. It still counts against
the `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts\n> REQUESTS and is **shared** with eval-run and user-testing insights, so a\n> request h

ere takes one from there too. Poll the `GET` rather than
> re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice.
>
>
Three refusals, three different meanings: a short `429` is the per-minute\n> brake (wait seconds), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay`
is the daily ledger\n> (its `Retry-After`, when present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403` means\n> the feature is not availab
le to your organization — waiting will never help.\n\n**User testing** (`/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/study`
,\n`.../studies/...`) — publishing an environment for real visitors, reading what\nthey did, and controlling who can reach it. A *

*study** is a published
environment: one per environment, addressed by its own id once it exists.

| Endpoint | What it does |\
n| - | - |\n| `PUT .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent — republishing returns the existing study, an
d `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |\n| `DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Unpublish.** The link dies
and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when there was nothing published |\n| `PATCH .../studies/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe,
or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions` | What visitors did: one row per session, with feedback and a first-me
ssage preview |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcript, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are
dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-execution` | The spend dial for anonymous visitors: daily credits, computer starts,
concurrency |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rotate-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No body — the new secret is minted server-
side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | Invite someone (or change their role) on an `invited_only` study |\n| `DELETE .../
studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Remove someone. Their grant is revoked, ending their live sessions |\n| `POST .../s

tudies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a different environment in the same project |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the l
ink does not evict anyone who already used it.** It stops the\n> old URL from granting NEW access; the grants already redeemed und
er it stay\n> valid. That is the single most important thing to know here, because rotation\n> is what you reach for when a link l

eaks — and on its own it does not undo the
> leak. Rotate *and* remove the members you did not intend to have.
>
> What DOES ta
ke effect at once, ending live sessions rather than waiting for\n> expiry: unpublishing, tightening `mode`, and removing a member.
Those bump\n> the study's `accessVersion`, and a session minted under an older version\n> stops working. None of them reverse by

calling the opposite — a re-invited
> member gets a new session, not their old one.
>
> Read `accessVersion` off the publish an

d rebind responses. The update and
> rotate responses do not carry it.

**User testing — what visitors did** — the analytics re
ads, and the model pass\nover them. Read these in cost order: metrics, usage and signals are\ndeterministic and free; the insights

request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and
feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which
models, tools and servers the sessions used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sig
nals` | What the miner found in the current window — and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/findings` |
Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/windows/{windowId}/insights` | One w
indow's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **
No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the window has not been mined yet |\n|
`DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId` in the body |\n| `POST .../studie
s/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it stays dismissed when insights regener

ate |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usage` response includes an `analysis`
summary: `total`, `analyzed`,\n`pending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` describe session\ncoverage. Failure/skip
reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `staleAssignments` distinguish catalog
\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe\nthe map independently. Reading this response neve

r starts analysis.

Taxonomy entries carry the published version and discovery status. Theme ids
remain stable across additions
and cosmetic renames. An older assignment\nversion can still be valid when its theme is unchanged; a retired or replaced\nmembers
hip remains visible while cached reassignment completes. These are\ncurrent views with version provenance, not historical traffic

snapshots.

Check `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a
whole-scope total. Map reads separa
tely expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsampling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed counts cover only its requested\ngoa
